name: bossku-ai
notes: The file is at packages/bossku-ai/skills/bossku-ai/SKILL.md and is a Codex-specific skill entry point. BosskuAI provides scripts/install.sh, which installs agent rules, skills and configuration into other projects, so it acts as a reusable project setup tool.

name: azure-infra
notes: The repository README states that it converts OpenClaw skills into a Claude skills marketplace, that the plugins/ folder holds skills collected and converted from OpenClaw, and that the repository is a mirror and distribution collection of community skills.

name: story-readiness
notes: It mainly performs pre-implementation quality assurance: checking that acceptance criteria are clear and testable, verifying GDD requirements and ADR architecture references, checking dependencies, asset files and open design questions, verifying the definition of done and test evidence, and returning READY, NEEDS WORK or BLOCKED. So testing fits better than docs or agent-meta: it reads documents, but its main purpose is quality checking, not writing documents. GitHub marks the repository as a public template with preconfigured AI agents, skills, workflows and project structure for game development projects.

name: fork-terminal
notes: This skill is distributed as part of a reusable project scaffold.

name: twitter
notes: It uses the MediaUse CLI, but its main goal is social-media business tasks, not developing or maintaining software. The repository README says it manages MediaUse agent skills in one place, includes skills for Twitter, Instagram, Reddit, ChatGPT and other platforms, stores each platform's skill at <pluginName>/SKILL.md, and that the skills install into Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and Cursor.

name: podcast-generation
notes: The skill focuses on one task: turning text into podcast audio with the Azure OpenAI Realtime API. The repository is a large agent skills collection that gathers skills from many sources.
